alt: An abandoned cart is a question to investigate.
A left cart is not always a no. Someone added a product and left. Find out why before you cut your price.
Four things to check: Costs; Delivery; Trust; Payment
Investigate in order: Go through checkout - On your own phone.; Note the surprises - Anything a buyer might not expect.; Fix the cause - Then consider a discount.
Discount first vs answer first. Discount first: May hide the real problem; Costs you margin. Investigate first: Finds the real reason; Discount only if needed
Ask, if they agreed to hear from you. A short, polite message to someone who left a cart can teach you more than guessing.
Check your checkout: Is the total clear early?; Is the delivery time stated?; Does the page feel trustworthy?; Does payment work smoothly?

caption:
An abandoned cart is a question to investigate. 🛒

When someone adds a product and leaves, the first reaction is often a discount. But the real reason may be something else: extra costs that appear late, unclear delivery time, a page that does not feel trustworthy, or a payment step that does not work smoothly.

Go through your own checkout on your phone, note every surprise, fix the cause, and only then consider a discount. If customers agreed to hear from you, a short polite message can also teach you a lot.
